key_insight: By engineering the film morphology of chiral 2D perovskite R-(MBA)2PbI4, the authors enabled the first robust lateral electrical and magnetotransport measurements in a material previously too resistive to characterize in-plane.
engineering_relevance: This shows that morphology control can unlock device-level transport in chiral perovskites, opening a path toward spintronic and optoelectronic integration beyond solar-cell-oriented thin films.
method: Optimized thin-film morphology of R-(MBA)2PbI4 to reduce in-plane transport bottlenecks.
Built Hall-bar devices for dark Hall and magnetotransport measurements.
Compared transport across paths with and without grain boundaries to probe morphology effects.
evidence_signal: Hall measurements in the dark identified p-type conduction with ~0.2 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1 mobility and ~3×10^14 cm^-2 carrier density, and transport paths crossing grain boundaries showed enhanced magnetoresistance.
watch_item: The measured in-plane mobility is still very low, so performance may remain strongly limited by grain boundaries and film quality in practical devices.
paper_title: Morphology control and low-temperature magnetotransport in chiral 2D perovskite R-(MBA)$_2$PbI$_4$
